visual.nota: Negative feedback keeps temperature near the daisies' optimum

turnos.t: The Gaia hypothesis: Earth is a single integrated, self-regulating system in which living organisms interact with their inorganic surroundings, through feedback, to maintain conditions suitable for life. Proposed by James Lovelock and Lynn Margulis in the 1970s.

A computer model of a planet with only black and white daisies. When it's cold, black daisies, with low albedo, absorb heat and spread, warming the planet. When it's warm, white daisies, with high albedo, spread and reflect light, cooling it. Even as the sun gets brighter, temperature stays near the optimum. Life itself provides the negative feedback.
